    Your graphics workspace

    Write. Run. Explore.

    This workspace runs real C and C++ code in your browser. Start a new program or open your own single source file.

    1. Open your code. Use New program for the starter source or Open file for an existing program.
    2. Edit the C/C++ source. Changes save automatically in this browser.
    3. Press Run. Compiler errors appear in the console. Click the canvas before using keyboard or mouse controls.

    What is supported?

    The graphics runtime implements a focused set of legacy OpenGL, GLU, and GLUT: immediate-mode shapes, colors, matrices, projections, depth, lighting, materials, standard GLUT geometry, callbacks, and menus. It uses WebGL to render the result.

    This is a teaching compatibility runtime, not a complete desktop OpenGL installation. Unsupported functions produce compile/link errors or runtime diagnostics. Native operating-system APIs, multiple windows, and external C/C++ packages are not included. Browser rendering can differ from your desktop, particularly line patterns and lighting.

    Standard output (printf and std::cout) appears in the console. For scanf or cin, open Input in the console and enter the values before pressing Run. Input is supplied once per run; it is not an interactive terminal.

    Keep your work

    Your programs are saved in this browser. Download your source before clearing browser data or switching devices. Importing a file opens it as your personal program.
